question: A man buys an article at 16 for ₹1,200 ad an equal number of articles at 12 for ₹960. He sells all the articles at 15 for ₹1,350. His profit percentage in the entire transaction is (correct to one decimal place):
solution:
Given:

A man buys an article at 16 for ₹1,200 and an equal number of articles at 12 for ₹960. 

He sells all the articles at 15 for ₹1,350.

Concept used:

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\% 

Calculation:

LCM (16, 12, 15) = 240

Let the man bought 240Q articles at 16 for ₹1,200 and 240Q articles at 12 for ₹960.

Total number of articles = 240Q + 240Q = 480Q

The total cost price of the first category product

⇒ 240Q × (1200/16)

⇒ ₹18,000Q

The total cost price of the second category product

⇒ 240Q × (960/12)

⇒ ₹19,200Q

The total cost price of 480Q articles

⇒ 18,000Q + 19,200Q

⇒ ₹37,200Q

The total selling price of 480Q articles

⇒ 480Q × (1350/15)

⇒ ₹43,200Q

Now, profit% = {{43200Q - 37200Q} over 37200Q} times 100\%

⇒ {{6000} over 37200} times 100\%

⇒ 16.12% ≈ 16.1%

**∴ His profit percentage in the entire transaction is 16.1%.**
